subject.title: perf(logging): flush file transport asynchronously off the request path

question: Should OpenClaw’s default file logger trade synchronous per-record durability for a bounded queue that drops oldest records during overload?
rationale: This is an intentional operational contract change, not a purely internal refactor: file logs are used for diagnosis precisely during overloaded conditions.

options.title: Require loss-free default behavior
options.body: Keep the performance work but redesign the default path so accepted records are not discarded under normal overload handling.

options.title: Accept bounded loss explicitly
options.body: Approve the 4,096-record drop-oldest policy as the default and document the diagnostic durability tradeoff.

options.title: Defer the transport change
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose the desired durability and latency contract for file logging.

recommendation.title: Require loss-free default behavior
recommendation.body: Keep the performance work but redesign the default path so accepted records are not discarded under normal overload handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR’s production performance rationale and proposed logging lifecycle design make this the closest available routing candidate, although current-main ownership provenance remains low-confidence.
